variables_needed.referrer: data-collection site (36 sites); full names in OSF Table S1
variables_needed.sample: numeric site code, one-to-one with referrer
variables_needed.gainlossgroup: assigned frame: 1 = gain wording (item diseaseframinga), 0 = loss wording (item diseaseframingb)
variables_needed.gainlossDV: choice: 1 = program with exact (sure) outcome, 2 = probabilistic (risky) program; blank = no response
variables_needed.diseaseframinga: raw gain-frame item (1 = "200 people will be saved", 2 = risky)
variables_needed.diseaseframingb: raw loss-frame item (1 = "400 people will die", 2 = risky)

outcome_coding.chose_certain: gainlossDV == 1 (success); gainlossDV == 2 is the risky program (failure)

sources.wording: Codebook stem (both frames): "Imagine that the United States is preparing for the outbreak of an unusual disease, which is expected to kill 600 people. Two alternative programs to fight the disease have been proposed. Choose program:". Options are given only as value-label summaries (gain: "200 people will be saved" / "1/3 probability to save all, 2/3 nobody will be saved"; loss: "400 people will die" / "1/3 probability nobody will die, 2/3 that 600 will die"). Non-English sites used translations not included in this file.
sources.reproducibility: Reproduced. Frame and choice codes agree row-for-row with the raw items; frame sizes match the Berkeley extract exactly; all 36 sites x 5 cells match the ML1 analysts' own Gain_Loss sheet (MLforR.xlsx).
discrepancies: Mixed text encoding: 297 of 6,346 physical lines contain bytes that are not valid UTF-8 (all in free-text columns). The file is read as UTF-8 with replacement characters; the audit checks that no column used here contains a replacement character.

Codebook value labels for gainlossgroup and gainlossDV are truncated inside the xlsx itself ("{,00, People will die}...", "{1,00, chose program with exact outcome}..."). The mapping is established from the raw items diseaseframinga/b and the check ml1_codebook_items, and is consistent with these truncated labels.

mturk.exclude (3 rows, values 2 and 99) and mturk.exclude.null (20 rows, value 1) flag 23 rows. All 23 answered the framing item, which contradicts the description "completed zero mini-experiments" for mturk.exclude.null. Neither the ML1 analysts' Gain_Loss sheet nor the Berkeley extract excludes them, so the published analysis set keeps them. The import keeps them and reports the flags (decision recorded in the import spec).

The stimulus wording in the ML1 codebook ("to fight the disease ... Choose program:") differs from Tversky & Kahneman (1981) ("to combat the disease ... Assume that the exact scientific estimates ... Which of the two programs would you favor?").
unknowns: Exact full option texts shown to ML1 participants (only abbreviated value labels here).
Translations used at non-English sites and which sites used them.

sources.exclusions: ML2 key table (unique.id 47) intends "Timing > 4" seconds but the entry is malformed (c('Timing > 4') instead of c('Timing', 'X > 4')); the published results report 0 excluded cases, and 100 rows have a page time under 4 s. No prior-exposure filter in Hauser.4 (that is Hauser.5/6).
sources.reproducibility: Reproduced (sealed check ml2_hauser4_results): N = 7,923, per-condition n, and Yes/No counts equal the published RESULTS file; the condition mapping and Yes/No coding agree with the raw items for every row.
discrepancies: The preregistered analysis plan (manylabRs varfun.Hauser.1 documentation) excludes participants who took fewer than 4 seconds; the published Hauser.4 analysis did not apply it (malformed key-table filter). The benchmark follows the published analysis (N = 7,923); the 4-second rule is available as a sealed sensitivity import.
The key table requests a one-sided test (alternative = 'greater'); the published RESULTS file reports a two-sided Fisher exact test.
In the RESULTS file, stat.cond3.n and stat.cond4.n (GreaterGood rows) show 3,955 (the SideEffect n); stat.n2 = 3,968 is correct and the GreaterGood proportions use 3,968.

manylabRs varfun.Hauser.2 (not used by Hauser.4) pairs SideEffect with haus3.1 in its code while its documentation pairs haus3.1 with GreaterGood. Hauser.4 uses varfun.Hauser.1 with the key-table mapping SideEffect = haus4.1, GreaterGood = haus3.1, which the data confirm.
unknowns: Exact English wording presented by ML2 (ML2 materials not in hand); the 2007 Appendix text is used.
Translations used at the 11 non-English language sites.

sources.reproducibility: 4,149 respondents, 1,297 variables, all with year 2022. Value labels and missing codes are read from the file (`sim survey-personas` records counts per missing code with the file's own labels: e.g. .i iap = not asked, .d don't know, .r refused, .n no answer, .s skipped on web, .y not available in this year).
discrepancies: The configured weight (wtssps) exists only for the 3,544 baseline cross-section cases. NORC's release notes say the 605 AmeriSpeak oversample cases (Black, Hispanic and Asian respondents, same national frame) can be analyzed together with the rest only with WTSSPS_AS / WTSSNRPS_AS. Personas are therefore drawn from the baseline sample. Use of wtssps_as would require a preregistered change.
